findings.title: Hostility as an Adhesive Relation
findings.claim: The focus causative action makes hostility adhere within the group's between-space, so enmity and hatred become a durable hostile relation as well as an antagonistic placement.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 5:14:13:2 meets the internal relation at 5:14:14:1 and the paired definite objects at 5:14:15:2 and 5:14:16:3. The adhesive facet supplies sticking, while the inciting facet supplies setting parties against one another; together they change the result from hostility merely occurring among people to hostility binding the relation in which they stand.
findings.reader_payoff: The two hostile nouns can be seen as a force that holds the group in antagonism, making the placement of hostility itself part of the social mechanism.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading that enmity and hatred are placed among them remains intact. The adhesive branch is used as a bounded contextual image of sticking and does not reparse the Form IV carrier as a noun for glue; the inciting and adhesive images remain co-present without ranking one over the other.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and branch facets are directly supplied and the candidate support is trusted, but the channel record is a nomination and the adhesive relation is an interpretive synthesis rather than a lexical replacement.
